findings: Non-initiating callers (the `else` branch) only `sleep(50)` once and then unconditionally return whatever `currentToken` currently holds — they never re-check whether the in-flight refresh actually completed, and there is no shared promise/queue at the call sites (the file explicitly says every request calls `getToken()` independently). Since refresh is a network round trip typically well over 50ms, these callers systematically return the same token that was already judged expired by the caller that triggered the refresh, so their authenticated request fails and the app surfaces this as a logout. This is the primary root cause of the 'intermittent logout' reports, with severity scaling with request concurrency and refresh latency.

`await refreshToken(oldToken)` has no try/catch/finally. If the refresh call throws or rejects (any transient network/server error), `refreshing` is never reset to `false` and `currentToken` is never updated to a new value. Every subsequent `getToken()` call then permanently falls into the 'wait and return stale token' branch, because no future call will ever see `refreshing === false` and attempt another refresh. A single transient refresh failure therefore converts into a permanent, session-wide auth livelock that only a full page reload (resetting module state) can clear — this is a distinct defect from the polling race and explains why some logouts are unrecoverable rather than truly transient.

The comment states the server invalidates `oldToken` the instant it receives the `/auth/refresh` POST, i.e. before the refresh response (and therefore the new token) is even available client-side. Combined with the architecture where every authenticated request calls `getToken()' independently with no shared in-flight-request tracking, any other request that grabbed the still-valid old token just before a refresh was triggered elsewhere on the page can fail collaterally the moment the refresh request lands server-side — a structural race between token invalidation and concurrent in-flight request usage that is not mitigated anywhere in this code.
